newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - All eyes on the consumer.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - All eyes on the consumer.

text.p: UK gilts face a tough test this week from crucial data covering the lively consumer sector and key international events as both the FOMC and Bundesbank meet.
Gilts pushed up in early Monday trade and outperformed other markets as July PSBR data painted a brighter-than-expected picture of the public finances.
But retail sales data on Wednesday will be crucial in determining whether or not the market can hold on to its optimistic outlook for interest rates.
"Without doubt Wednesday's retail sales figure stands head and shoulders above the other economic numbers this week," said Don Smith, strategist at HSBC Markets.
"Concerns about rampant consumer spending are crucial in influencing the market's perceptions about interest rate prospects."

The market and the Bank of England are concerned that robust consumer spending, driven by higher earnings and one-off windfall payments from building society conversions, will allow high street shops to ratchet up their prices.

The Reuter consensus forecast suggests retail sales rose by 0.3 percent in July compared with June's 0.6 percent, although this would push the year-on-year rate of growth up to 5.8 percent from 5.4 in June.
Smith said the market would view the risks on the upside, but if the data shows the pace of sales growth easing, the long end would be the chief beneficiary.

"(If the figures are soft), longs would outperform, especially if investors begin to ponder on the possibility that the economy, inflation and interest rates could weaken significantly next year," he said.

The long end outperformed last week, largely reversing a spate of underperformance the week before after the Bank of England raised rates and hinted that it might be the last tightening for some time.
Graham McDevitt, fixed income strategist at Paribas Capital Markets, said the short sterling strip's optimistic view on interest rates was helping support the whole curve.
The strip is discounting just one more quarter-point rate rise this cycle.
"The market has decided that a lot of the necessary monetary tightening has already taken place. That will help gilts sustain these levels," said McDevitt.

But he said the market could face a few tricky months as the economic data comes in against a background of rates on hold. "I would not forecast the spread narrowing much in the course of the next few month as a result."
The spread stood at 149 basis points on Monday compared with 151 on Friday, largely a result of the favourable PSBR data.
That showed record VAT receipts contributed to a repayment of 3.875 billion stg in July, much higher than the 1.9 billion repayment forecast.
International figures will also play a large part in gilts' performance this week.
The Bundesbank holds its regular repo on Tuesday, then the policy setting council reconvenes after the summer break on Thursday.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday. Few economists forecast a monetary tightening at either meeting, but markets will be jittery ahead of the announcements.

"The feeling is there won't be any move in rates at either meeting, but the risk of an adverse reaction is greater if the Bundesbank moves," said one gilts trader. "And it's only a matter of time before the cycle turns." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7715
